items.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
items.summary: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. items.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
items.summary: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. items.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
items.summary: Code localizers are usually trained to predict the files a reference patch edits, but the code a fixer needs to read is not the same as the code it changes. items.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
items.summary: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. items.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
items.summary: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process. Weight merging and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) must re-consolidate the whole model whenever an expert is added, and can erode capabilities outside the target domains. items.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
items.summary: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both interactive worlds and the tasks agents must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation (WD). items.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
items.summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. items.summary: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. items.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
items.summary: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. items.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
items.summary: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models. items.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
items.summary: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. items.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
items.summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. items.title: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains coding agents on software tasks whose hidden tests decide the reward, yet task collections check these tests only against the reference fix. We ask what makes a task good training data, focusing on the correctness of its reward labels. We audit SWE-Gym with two LLM families, and a suspected error counts only if execution reproduces it. items.title: Beam Model Technical Report
items.summary: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. items.title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction
items.summary: Effective real-time, full-duplex multimodal interaction requires systems to understand not only what users say, but also the communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and to generate audiovisual responses that appropriately address those needs. items.title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
items.summary: Latent generative models typically rely on three separate networks: an encoder that tokenizes pixels, a generator that models the latent distribution, and a decoder that maps latents back to pixels. items.title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. items.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
items.summary: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. items.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. items.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
items.summary: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. items.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. items.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
items.summary: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. items.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
items.summary: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. items.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object.
